title: Celeriac and butter bean pot with pollock

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a cupboard staple; vegetable stock counts as good stock and tinned butter beans are allowed.

supermarket.reason: Celeriac, pollock fillets, kale, mushrooms and tinned butter beans are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole and a sieve, and the techniques are frying, simmering and steaming fish on top.

works.reason: 600g celeriac, two tins of beans, 500ml stock and four fillets give a sensible brothy pot for four, and the 15-minute simmer and 6–8 minutes for the fish are realistic.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers peeling and cubing the celeriac and slicing the onion, mushrooms, garlic and kale, and 8+15+8 minutes matches the 30 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, including the lemon and the seasoned pollock, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm celeriac and bean pot suits 22 December, and 600g of celeriac makes it the backbone of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, beans and plenty of vegetables make a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
